Chapter 8: Sustaining Momentum Through Seasons of Change
You know, life really does move in seasons. There are times of growth, moments of rest, periods of challenge, and those beautiful stretches of renewal.
If you want to keep your momentum going in the long run, you’ve got to find a way to move with these natural rhythms, instead of pushing against them. What works when you’re full of energy and everything feels stable, well, that might not be possible when you’re dealing with big changes or extra stress.
So, how do you actually honor these different seasons in your life? Let’s break it down.
First, try honestly assessing your current capacity. Think about how much time, energy, and support you really have right now. If you’re overwhelmed or going through a tough patch, it’s perfectly fine to scale back. Maybe this is a time for maintenance—just keeping things steady—instead of pushing for big growth.
Next up, let’s talk about adjusting your expectations. Success isn’t a one-size-fits-all thing. In some seasons, maintaining your healthy habits or staying true to what matters most is a huge win. Give yourself permission to redefine what achievement looks like, depending on where you are in life.
And here’s something that really makes a difference: building in time for rest and reflection. Actually schedule those breaks to recharge. Pausing now and then not only helps you avoid burnout, but it also opens up space for fresh ideas and creativity.
Picture this—a parent welcoming a new baby home. In that season, it makes sense to shift focus away from big career ambitions and concentrate on family and self-care. Later, as things settle down and routines get smoother, there’s room to ramp up those professional goals again.
Through it all, sustaining momentum is about celebrating progress in every season, not just when you’re making giant leaps. Persistence, adaptability, and taking care of yourself—they’re the real building blocks of lasting success.
So, remember to notice and appreciate your growth, however it shows up, and let yourself move with the seasons of your own life.
